questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals of Concavity of a Function
questions.problem:
Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{2}-\frac{1}{x}$ defined on $x\in (0,\infty ).$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $f(x)$ is concave up on $(0,1)$
- $f(x)$ is concave down on $(0,1)$
- $f(x)$ is concave down on $(1,\infty )$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the second derivative of $f(x),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =2x+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =2-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the function is concave up, we need to solve ${f}^{″}(x)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}} & >0 \\ 2 & >\frac{2}{{x}^{3}} \\ {x}^{3} & >1 \\ x & >1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that $x>0.$

Hence, ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ when $x>1.$ So the graph is concave up on the interval $(1,\infty ).$

The function $f(x)$ is concave down when ${f}^{″}(x)<0.$ By similar reasoning to before, this leads to the inequality $2-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}<0,$ which has the solution $(0,1).$

Therefore, the correct answer is " II only."

choices.value: None of the statements are true.

questions.problem:
Consider the function $f(x)=3{x}^{5}-5{x}^{4}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $f(x)$ is concave down on $(1,\infty )$
- $f(x)$ is concave up on $(-\infty ,0)$
- $f(x)$ is concave up on $(1,\infty )$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the second derivative of $f(x),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =15{x}^{4}-20{x}^{3} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =60{x}^{3}-60{x}^{2} \\  & =60{x}^{2}(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the function is concave up, we need to solve ${f}^{″}(x)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}60{x}^{2}(x-1) & >0 \\ x-1 & >0 \\ x & >1\end{aligned}
$$

So $f(x)$ is concave up on the interval   $(1,\infty ).$

The function $f(x)$ is concave down when ${f}^{″}(x)<0.$ By similar reasoning, this leads to the inequality $x-1<0$ with $x\ne 0,$ which has the solution $(-\infty ,0)\cup (0,1).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
